name: The Animals We Wiped Out
description: The dodo, the great auk, the thylacine and the passenger pigeon: how hunting, new predators and lost habitats ended species, from the Ice Age to living memory.

checkpoints.name: The first hunters
checkpoints.note: After humans spread across the world, mammoths, giant sloths and many other large animals disappear, though climate change shares the blame.

checkpoints.name: Islands and empires
checkpoints.note: Roman demand ends silphium, and the first settlers of Madagascar and New Zealand hunt the elephant birds and moa to extinction.

checkpoints.name: The age of sail and the gun
checkpoints.note: Sailors kill off the dodo, the sea cow and the great auk, and market hunters shoot the passenger pigeon and the quagga.

checkpoints.name: Modern losses
checkpoints.note: The last passenger pigeon, thylacine and Pinta tortoise die, and more species go because of pollution, poaching, disease and habitat loss.
